title: Do Auctioneers Pick Optimal Reserve Prices?

source.title: Do Auctioneers Pick Optimal Reserve Prices?
source.authors: Andrew M. Davis, Elena Katok, Anthony M. Kwasnica

studies.title: Original auction · Distributions and bidder information

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How do sellers set a minimum acceptable price when the number of potential bidders changes?

fields.label: What the paper covers
fields.value: The original Davis, Katok and Kwasnica experiment crossed bidder-value distributions with information conditions. The later Bench agent task covers a narrower setting.

fields.label: Across the paper
fields.value: Sellers increased their reserve prices as bidder counts rose, including in treatments where the standard benchmark predicts a constant reserve.

fields.label: Expectation or comparison
fields.value: Under the standard benchmark the optimal reserve is independent of bidder count for a given distribution. The treatments probe why sellers might depart from that benchmark.

fields.label: Interpretation and limits
fields.value: The separate Feng benchmark is not a finding from this paper. The one-decision Bench adapter does not reproduce the original multi-round seller task.
fields.derivation: Scope of the published evidence and, where linked, differences from the Bench adaptation.

fields.label: Participants, procedure and measures
fields.value: 120 sellers participated across treatment cells that varied the bidder-value distribution and what sellers knew. Sellers set reserve prices across rounds with different bidder counts. The value distribution changes the theoretical optimal reserve; standard theory predicts it is independent of the number of bidders.

fields.label: Result
fields.value: The authors compare reserve prices with standard theory and use information treatments to test explanations for why sellers respond to bidder count.

fields.label: Participants, procedure and measures
fields.value: The NoInfo regression covers 80 of the 120 sellers. FullInfo treatments are analyzed separately. The dependent variable is the seller’s reserve price.

fields.label: Result
fields.value: The NoInfo table reports a positive coefficient of 2.98 (SE 0.08, p<.01) for bidder count in its initial pooled specification. The original study reports reserve prices rising with bidder count in cases where the standard benchmark predicts a constant reserve.
